I said fifteen, not fifty.
Would you like coffee or tea?
Sorry, I didn't catch that.
Could you say it again, a little slower?

Hi, I'm Li Ming. Nice to meet you.
I'm a second-year student in the English Department.
In my free time I like playing badminton and watching documentaries.
Anyway, it was nice talking to you. See you around.

Good evening. A table for two, please.
I'll have the chicken salad, please.
Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the train station?
Is it within walking distance? Thank you.

Good morning. I'd like to check in for the flight to Boston.
Could I have an aisle seat, please?
I have one suitcase. Also, I have a reservation under the name Li, for two nights.

Hello, this is Li Ming speaking.
Could I speak to Mr. Brown, please?
I'm afraid I have to reschedule our appointment.
Would Thursday morning be possible?
Could you ask him to call me back?

Excuse me, Professor. Could I ask a question about the reading?
Sorry, I didn't quite follow. Would you mind going over it again?
That's a good point, but I see it a bit differently.

Good morning, everyone. Just a quick update on the report.
We've finished the first draft, but we're still waiting for the client's feedback.
I'll send it out by Friday.
Could I add one more thing?

That's a good point, but have we considered the cost?
I see what you mean, but I'm not sure it would work in practice.
I'm afraid I disagree.
Maybe we could look at the numbers together.

Good morning. My name is Li Ming, and I'm a second-year student at Nanjing University, majoring in Business English.
In my free time I enjoy playing badminton.
I'm glad to be here today.

Today I'd like to talk about part-time jobs for students.
In my opinion, a part-time job is helpful, as long as it doesn't affect our study.
That's a good question. Let me think for a second.
